source: He & Wang (2025) When do symbolic solvers enhance reasoning in LLMs? (NeurIPS 2025 workshop)
finding: With GPT-4o, chain-of-thought (CoT) beats code-plus-solver on shallow items. A solver route wins only on search-heavy constraint puzzles. Answers gap 1 and gap 5 in part.
numbers: GPT-4o CoT: GSM8K 94.6, GSM-Reversed 90.3, GSM-Hard 69.1, EntailmentBank 81.8. ZebraLogic (1000 puzzles, 2x2 to 6x6) CoT easy/hard/avg 77.9/8.9/28.2. One-shot declarative Prolog 96.8/44.0/58.8. One-shot declarative Python+constraint library 96.4/62.1/71.7. Claude 3.5 Sonnet CoT avg 32.6.
quote: only helps when the problem requires limited implicit reasoning but involves an ample search space
limits: Table text extracted from the PDF is partly garbled; rows read by position. GPT-4o is a non-reasoning model. Zero-shot Prolog on EntailmentBank is far below CoT (one cell reads 27.4). Greedy decoding, up to 10 retries. No FOLIO, ProverQA or AR-LSAT.
agent_relevance: Gate the solver route on search-heavy constraint structure, not on 'logic' in general. On shallow deduction and word problems keep CoT.

source: He & Wang (2025) retry ablation (Table 3 and Fig. 3)
finding: Retries are a real part of the cost of translate-and-solve. Prolog needs more retries than Python. A declarative one-shot example removes most of the need. Answers gap 2 in part.
numbers: GPT-4o accuracy at max 1/2/10 attempts, GSM-Hard: Prolog zero-shot 49/63/71; Prolog one-shot 73/77/78; Python zero-shot 75/76/76; Python one-shot 71/73/73. ZebraLogic (160 mid-size puzzles) Prolog one-shot 83/83/83, Python one-shot 84/84/84. CodeLlama-13B Python one-shot 32/35/41. Prolog zero-shot: 80 of 1319 GSM-Hard problems still not executable after 10 attempts.
limits: Retries triggered only by interpreter syntax errors, not by wrong meaning. Token counts per call not reported.
agent_relevance: Budget 1 to 3 repair rounds for syntax. Further rounds add little once a worked example is in the prompt.

source: Bansal, Kurniawan & Frermann (2025) Robustness of neurosymbolic reasoners on first-order logic problems
finding: On the full FOLIO validation set (N=204) CoT beats LINC for all five open models tested. The hybrid NSCoT (CoT first, then FOL translation) beats LINC but still trails CoT. Answers gap 1 in part (open models only) and gap 4 in part.
numbers: FOLIO validation accuracy (Naive / CoT / LINC / NSCoT): Mistral-7B 53.43/56.37/52.94/53.92; Qwen2.5-7B 59.31/70.59/58.33/66.67; Qwen2.5-32B 66.18/75.49/68.14/71.08; Llama-3.1-8B 33.33/70.59/58.33/68.14; Gemma-3-12B 64.22/77.45/57.35/63.24. Naive prompting beat LINC on 3 of 5 models.
quote: NSCoT consistently lags behind the CoT baseline
limits: Open models of 7B to 32B, not frontier. The authors note the small counterfactual set (from Wu et al. 2024) gave a different picture from the full set and suspect its selection heuristics. LINC with GPT-4 not rerun.
agent_relevance: At open-model scale a plain solver route loses to CoT on FOLIO. Let CoT write its reasoning before any formal step.

source: Bansal et al. (2025) premise-count analysis and counterfactual robustness
finding: Neurosymbolic methods are more robust to counterfactual swaps of nouns, but less accurate overall. LINC falls faster than NSCoT as the number of premises grows (2 to 8) on FOLIO.
numbers: Counterfactual set RR (81 items): LINC and NSCoT show small non-significant default-vs-counterfactual gaps; some CoT and naive baselines show gaps of roughly 12 to 30 points (McNemar p<0.05 marked brittle). Exact per-model cells not reliably readable from the PDF text.
limits: Small set (81 items), FOLIO-derived only.
agent_relevance: Robustness is the one reproducible benefit of the solver route against surface changes. Use it as a consistency check, not as the main answer path.

source: Callewaert, Vandevelde & Vennekens (2025) VERUS-LM: a versatile framework combining LLMs with symbolic reasoning
finding: A generic-prompt pipeline with the FO(.)/IDP-Z3 solver matches other solver systems on four benchmarks and clearly beats them on AR-LSAT. Self-refinement raises the execution rate more than it raises correctness. Answers gap 1 and gap 2 in part for AR-LSAT.
numbers: Accuracy VERUS-LM / Logic-LM(GPT-4): PrOntoQA 95.8/83.20; ProofWriter 93.83/78.80; FOLIO 78.43/68.55; LogicalDeduction 88.67/87.63; AR-LSAT 68.36/23.40. GPT-4 CoT on AR-LSAT about 33 to 35 (rows are interleaved in the PDF text; Logic-LM paper gives 35.06). FOLIO refinement (total accuracy): none 57.8, syntax-only 74.0, syntax+semantic 78.4; execution rate 71.6 to 89.2 to 100; execution accuracy 80.8 to 80.6 to 78.4. AR-LSAT: 50.8 to 64.0 to 68.4; execution accuracy fell 84.3 to 69.3.
limits: GPT-4-era model. Only the AR-LSAT and FOLIO figures used because other rows are interleaved. No CoT fallback. Authors admit there is no way to validate formula correctness.
agent_relevance: On hard multi-constraint items a solver route with a rich formalism is a real gain over CoT. Semantic repair makes more programs run but not more programs right.

source: VERUS-LM task-type classifier (same paper, Tables 2 and 5)
finding: A small fine-tuned BERT classifier can name the inference type needed (entailment, satisfiability, range, optimisation, propagation) from the question text. This is the only routing signal found. Answers gap 5 in part.
numbers: BERT classifier trained on over 1000 labelled questions: average accuracy 92.6% on the custom task set. AR-LSAT detected-task mix and execution accuracy: Entailment 45.89% (66.04), Satisfiability 31.17% (69.01), Determine range 16.88% (79.49), Optimisation 6.06% (71.43).
limits: Routes among solver inference modes, not between solver and CoT. In-house training data. No test of whether depth or constraint count predicts when the solver beats CoT.
agent_relevance: A cheap gate is possible for task type. A gate for 'solver vs CoT' still has no evidence beyond the He & Wang pattern.

source: Ishay & Lee (2026) LLMs as ASP programmers: self-correction enables task-agnostic nonmonotonic reasoning (ACL Findings)
finding: With current reasoning models, translating to Answer Set Programming (clingo) with solver feedback beats the same model reasoning alone on average, and by a lot on hard constraint tasks. Answers gap 1 in part and gap 6 in part.
numbers: Average over 7 task columns, baseline to LLM+ASP (compact reference): Gemini 2.5 Pro 62.9 to 93.9; Gemini 2.5 Flash 43.3 to 86.9; o4-mini 63.4 to 82.3; DeepSeek-R1-0528 52.3 to 81.9; DeepSeek-V3 34.3 to 45.0; mean 51.3 to 78.0. ZL-XXL mean 24.2 to 71.3. SudokuBench 8.4 to 59.8. Mystery Blocksworld 64.2 to 72.6. MultiLogicNMR skeptical 59.0 to 90.5, credulous 52.9 to 81.0.
quote: even strong o4-mini (63.4%) reaches 82.3% with ASP
limits: No FOLIO, ProverQA or AR-LSAT: the sets are puzzle, planning and nonmonotonic tasks. Three runs with spread reported. Baseline is the model alone, not a CoT matched on token budget.
agent_relevance: For constraint-heavy puzzles and planning, a solver route beats frontier reasoning models. Strongest 2026 support for S2 with a solver.

source: Ishay & Lee (2026) token and call cost (RQ1, RQ3)
finding: The solver loop uses fewer tokens per correct answer on hard items, and its token use keeps growing with difficulty while baseline reasoning models give up. Revisions are the main cost. Answers gap 2 in part.
numbers: Mean revisions 2.18; mean runtime 2.3 s. Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.45 revisions; DeepSeek-V3 5.43. Without revisions mean accuracy 54.6; with revisions 78.0. On 12x12 Zebra, Gemini 2.5 Pro+ASP got 100% with about 25,000 tokens; the baseline used similar tokens and got 0%. Reference text in prompt: 22k tokens (full clingo manual) vs 2.6k tokens (compact guide).
limits: Total token bill for the pipeline is shown only in figures, not a table. The 25,000-token figure is one cell (12x12). The guide is paid on every call.
agent_relevance: Expect about 2 to 3 LLM calls per item plus a fixed reference prompt. On hard items this beat long CoT; on easy items it may cost more than plain CoT. Measure both.

source: Ishay & Lee (2026) false-accept rate of the LLM judge (Table 4)
finding: The loop ends when the same model says PASS on the solver output. That judge is wrong a noticeable share of the time, and worse for weaker models. This bears on G5 (no self-judged fixes). Answers gap 3 in part.
numbers: Incorrect PASS rate: Gemini 2.5 Pro 5.06% (50/989); Gemini 2.5 Flash 8.76% (86/982); o4-mini 12.42% (119/958); DeepSeek-R1-0528 13.86% (130/938); DeepSeek-V3 37.33% (249/667). Final errors in ZL-XL, ZL-XXL, SudokuBench with revisions: 18 syntax, 9 timeout, 127 satisfiable-but-wrong, 104 unsatisfiable.
limits: The judge sees the solver's answer set, so it judges an output, not a translation. Unsat-core tools proposed as future work, not tested.
agent_relevance: Do not let the translating model approve its own program. Use a checker that sees solver output or an independent re-derivation.

source: Ishay & Lee (2026) ASP vs SMT, and effect of reference text (RQ2, RQ4)
finding: The choice of formalism matters. SMT does better on plain constraint puzzles (more Z3 training data), but fails on default and exception reasoning, where ASP wins. A short rule guide beats a long manual. Answers gap 8 in part and gap 6 in part.
numbers: Zero-shot, no reference, with revisions: ZL-XL SMT 84.0 vs ASP 75.2; ZL-XXL 72.2 vs 56.2; Mystery Blocksworld 60.6 vs 53.2; SudokuBench 60.0 vs 60.8. MultiLogicNMR skeptical ASP 92.9 vs SMT 35.8; credulous 84.3 vs 35.0 (chance 33.3). BoardgameQA ASP 82.1 vs SMT 60.1. SMT on nonmonotonic tasks was below the LLM alone (59.0 and 52.9). Reference ablation (4 puzzle sets, average): none 61.4, standard 70.0, compact 73.1. Syntax errors on ZL-XXL: 84, 41, 16.
limits: No Datalog, Horn-only or DL arm, so fragment choice (gap 8) is covered only as classical vs nonmonotonic. Zero-shot setting.
agent_relevance: If S2 must hold exceptions and defaults, plain FOL or SMT is the wrong target. A short guide to the target language is worth its tokens.

source: Ishay & Lee (2026) BoardgameQA and defeasible rules
finding: When defeasible rules come with an explicit priority order, frontier LLMs already do well, and ASP adds nothing on average. ASP helps when the task needs world enumeration (skeptical vs credulous). Answers gap 6 in part.
numbers: BoardgameQA: ASP average 82.4 vs baseline 84.7. Reasoning models only: 92.0 vs 88.0. Gemini 2.5 Flash 93.0 baseline vs 94.7 with ASP; DeepSeek-V3 71.3 to 44.0.
limits: BoardgameQA is from 2023, so contamination is possible (the authors say so). Rules and facts are still given in text; missing-fact or implicit-rule cases not tested.
agent_relevance: Defeasible rules with stated priority need no solver. Use ASP only when the answer depends on comparing several consistent worlds.

source: Amrollahi, Lopez & Barrett (2026) Faithful autoformalization via roundtrip verification and repair
finding: Round-trip check: formalise, translate back to text, formalise again, and test equivalence of the two formal versions with an SMT solver. It needs no gold label and no human. A diagnosis step then picks which stage to repair. Answers gap 3 in part.
numbers: 150 Texas Transportation Code rules and 77 Parks and Wildlife rules; Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.2. Rules passing equivalence with no repair: 44.7% (Traffic/Claude) to 67.1% (Wildlife/GPT). After up to 3 repair rounds, Traffic/Claude: none 67 (44.7%), random-stage 100 (66.7%), regenerate 97 (64.7%), diagnosis-guided full 128 (85.3%). Wildlife/Claude 48 (62.3%) to 66 (85.7%). With Claude as diagnoser for GPT: 136/150 (90.7%) and 72/77 (94.7%). LLM calls per repair 6 to 26 depending on method (7.21 for Claude full vs 19.90 regenerate on Traffic).
limits: Statute rules in many-sorted FOL, not general reasoning questions. Equivalence is heuristic; two errors can cancel. GPT blamed stage 1 in 83% (Traffic) and 97% (Wildlife) of iterations, so diagnosis was biased. Repair is done by an LLM (a G5 concern), but the equivalence test is external.
agent_relevance: A solver-checked back-translation test is a gold-free detector of mistranslation. Cost is 3 translations per item plus repairs.

source: Amrollahi et al. (2026) does equivalence predict real faithfulness? (Tables 4, 6, 7)
finding: Rules that fail the round trip are more often semantically off. The signal is useful but not clean. Answers gap 3 in part.
numbers: NLI drift (unrelated or contradiction) is 1.45x to 2.52x higher for non-equivalent rules (pooled 2.03x under full repair; 1.78x over all 14 rows; 1.59x before any repair: 15.1% (39/258) vs 24.1% (47/195)). Human check on 25 rules: equivalent rules faithful 13/14 (93%), 1 minor; non-equivalent rules faithful 8/11 (73%), 3 minor, 0 unfaithful.
limits: Human judge was one author. Only 25 rules. The drift measure is an NLI model, itself a learned judge. Negation inversion and conditional thresholds were the common hidden errors.
agent_relevance: Round trip catches some errors but misses others and flags some good ones. Pair it with test cases rather than rely on it alone.

source: McGinness & Baumgartner (2024) Automated theorem provers help improve LLM reasoning
finding: A theorem-prover-based fixer (SEDAC) repairs semantic mistranslation, but the strongest fix needs a reference formalisation. Answers gap 3 in part.
numbers: PrOntoQA steamroller, 100 problems, 3 trials. Accuracy GPT-3 / GPT-4 / Gemini-Pro: normal 0.48/0.83/0.47; CoT one-shot 0.65/0.94/0.74; Fusemate logic program 0.66/0.94/0.57; plus one-shot 0.76/0.94/0.67; plus syntax fix 0.83/0.95/0.74; plus partial semantic fix 0.87/0.983/0.77; plus full semantic fix 0.98/0.995/0.96. Syntax fix removed 15 to 30% of errors; partial semantic fix 45 to 72%; full fix 88 to 92%.
limits: Full fix uses the correct natural-language axioms as reference, so it is an upper bound, not a deployable method. One synthetic domain. 2024 models. GPT-4 already reaches 0.94 with CoT one-shot.
agent_relevance: A partial fix without gold gave 45 to 72% fewer errors on a synthetic set. Real-text effect unknown.

source: Beiser, Penz & Musliu (2025) Intermediate languages matter
finding: The target language changes accuracy. FOL and NLTK beat ASP, and ASP beats Pyke (a Prolog-like rule engine), averaged over six models. Meaningful predicate names add about 13 points. Answers gap 8 and gap 9 in part.
numbers: Average overall accuracy on ProntoQA and ProofWriter, 6 LLMs, 8 prompt scenarios (n=80 per language): Pyke 44.55, ASP 56.40, NLTK 61.44, FOL 63.92. Predicate names: meaningful text 58.42 vs enumerated 45.49 (n=200). Comments and markdown: no clear effect. ASP execution rate 72.27 to 87.41%.
limits: ProntoQA and ProofWriter are synthetic and shallow. FOL vs NLTK and NLTK vs ASP not significant after correction. ASP errors: models mix strong negation (-) and default negation (not). Prompted models only; no Datalog or description-logic arm.
agent_relevance: Give predicates plain-language names. A dialect with unusual syntax costs accuracy; prefer a language the model has seen a lot.

source: Beiser et al. (2025) baselines on FOLIO and small-model solver failure
finding: Reproduced Logic-LM and LINC prompts fail almost entirely on syntax with a small model, while CoT stays strong. Shows how much solver-route results depend on model size and output format. Answers gap 1 in part.
numbers: Ministral-8B table: Standard/CoT overall accuracy ProntoQA 48.80/86.60, ProofWriter 47.33/51.67, FOLIO 54.90/60.78 (chance 50.00, 33.33, 33.33). Logic-LM* and LINC*: ProntoQA 2.20 and 6.20, ProofWriter 0.00 and 5.00, FOLIO 0.00 and 1.96 overall; execution rates 0 to 13.67%. The best neurosymbolic arms came within 10% of the baseline on FOLIO for 3 of 6 models.
limits: One small model in that table. The collapse is mostly a format failure (markdown bold around predicates), not reasoning failure. Output capped at 2048 tokens.
agent_relevance: The solver route needs a strict output format and a syntax-check loop, or small models never reach the solver.

source: Qi et al. (2025) ProverQA (ICLR 2025): chance level and prompting gain on the hard split
finding: Confirms ProverQA is three-way (True, False, Uncertain) and split by reasoning length. CoT adds little on the hard split. No solver arm was run. Answers gap 1 only as: no solver arm exists in this paper.
numbers: 1,500 items in three equal subsets: easy 1-2 steps, medium 3-5, hard 6-9. GPT-4o standard/CoT: easy 87.20/94.20, medium 68.60/79.40, hard 46.20/50.00. Claude-3.5-Sonnet: 85.00/95.20, 68.20/83.60, 42.80/56.40. Llama3.1-70B CoT hard 46.80. Mistral-Large CoT hard 52.20. Average CoT gain: easy 12.86, medium 8.43, hard 3.86.
limits: Chance for a 3-way label is 33.3% only if labels are balanced; the text I read does not state the label mix, so 'near chance' for the hard split is still unverified. Mid-2024 non-reasoning models. Items generated with Llama-3.1-70B and checked with a prover.
agent_relevance: The hard split is where CoT stalls near 50%, and a prover-backed route could help. Nobody has measured that.

source: Sprague et al. (2025) To CoT or not to CoT (ICLR 2025), Table 7 FOLIO rows
finding: Closes the layout question. The table header reads 'zero-shot CoT accuracy' then 'zero-shot DA accuracy', so the first column is CoT. CoT helps strongly on FOLIO for GPT-4o and gives mixed gains for others. Answers gap 10, first part.
numbers: FOLIO zero-shot CoT vs direct answer: GPT-4o 79.8 vs 62.6; Claude-3.5-Sonnet 73.9 vs 68.5; Gemini 1.5 Pro 73.9 vs 74.4; Gemini 1.5 Flash 74.9 vs 69.5; Llama-3.1-70B 70.9 vs 69.0; Llama-3.1-8B 58.6 vs 56.7; Llama 2 7B 36.5 vs 33.0.
quote: CoT primarily helps with the execution step
limits: 2024 non-reasoning models. Whether CoT still adds anything on FOLIO for models with long internal chains is not tested here.
agent_relevance: On FOLIO the CoT effect is model-dependent and can be zero. A solver-vs-CoT test needs a direct-answer arm too.

source: Szeider (2026) ASP-Bench: from natural language to logic programs
finding: With a ReAct agent that runs clingo in a loop, Claude Sonnet 4.5 solved every one of 128 natural-language ASP problems. Hard items cost many tool calls. Answers gap 2 in part.
numbers: 128 problems (64 base, easy and hard). All easy runs (2 each) and hard runs (3 each) correct. Mean 7.7 execution calls on hard problems (3.7 min, 26.0 max, DNA assembly). Hard 'who is the killer': 20 calls, about 622k input and 23k output tokens. Input:output token ratio rose from 24:1 (easy) to 45:1 (hardest). Time per call fell from 22 s to 15 s. Error correction under 10% of activities. The paper cites an earlier best of 58.5% on a 200-problem set.
limits: Agent prompt was tuned on the benchmark over several iterations. Reference validators check answers; in real use the agent's own checks are all there is. Saturation means the benchmark no longer separates systems.
agent_relevance: Agentic solver loops can saturate puzzle benchmarks but cost 100k to 600k input tokens on hard items. Compare with a CoT call before choosing.

source: He & Wang (2025) failure modes: implicit rules lost in translation (Sec. 6.4, Fig. 2)
finding: Translation into code drops rules that are implied by word meaning. CoT keeps them. This is the gap-6 failure shown on real text (EntailmentBank, GSM8K-Reversed).
numbers: EntailmentBank (300 items): CoT 81.8, Prolog far lower. On GSM8K and GSM-Reversed GPT-4o CoT scored above 90 and beat the solver arms.
limits: Two worked cases in a figure, not a counted error taxonomy. GPT-4o only.
agent_relevance: The solver route needs a step that lists implicit background rules before translation, or the missing rule becomes a silent wrong answer.
